title: Getting started
practice: Find three items in a small evidence set.

lessons.title: Meet the workspace
lessons.intro: A case is worked in the workspace. The evidence list sits on the left, the tools in the middle and your objectives, findings and notes on the right.

tryit.prompt: Put each thing where it lives in the workspace.
items: The list of items in the case

sandbox.task: Open the Timeline tab, then open the Findings panel on the right.

check.q: Where do you see what each stage needs you to do?
check.hint: It is in the side panel on the right.

check.q: What does the brief button show?
options: The case brief and messages from your case lead
check.hint: It sits in the top bar while a case is open.

options: No, only when you press Save
Yes, it autosaves as you work
Only when you close the program
check.hint: Look at the save status in the top bar.

lessons.title: The evidence list and viewers
lessons.intro: Every item opens in a viewer made for its type: tables, emails, phone extractions, images and documents. You always examine a working copy. The original stays sealed.

tryit.prompt: Click each covered field of this email to reveal what the headers say.
tryit.after: Headers say who sent an email, when, and where replies go. A Reply-To that differs from the sender is worth a closer look.

sandbox.task: Log receipt of the order record (EV-002), then examine a working copy of it.

steps.label: Examine a working copy of EV-002

check.q: Why do you examine a working copy?
options: So the original stays unchanged and can still be relied on
check.hint: Think about what would happen if the original changed.
Each type of item has its own viewer.

check.q: What does 'Not looked at' mean in the evidence list?
options: You have not examined it yet
check.hint: It changes once you examine the item.

lessons.title: Search and filters
lessons.intro: Search looks across every released item at once. Filters narrow the evidence list by type and status. Together they help you find the few items that matter among the noise.

tryit.prompt: Find three items: tick every item that mentions Linnet Close.
items: EV-002 Order record: 41 Linnet Close, Brackenfield
EV-005 Courier tracking: Delivered, Linnet Close

sandbox.task: Open the Search tab and search for 'Linnet'.

options: Only the item you have open
Every released item in the case

check.q: How do you see only the items you have not examined?
check.hint: The filters sit above the evidence list.

check.q: A case has plenty of irrelevant items. Why?
options: Real cases do too, and sorting signal from noise is a skill
check.hint: The amount of noise rises with difficulty.

lessons.title: Notes, findings and saving
lessons.intro: Notes are your private working space. Findings are the statements you will stand behind, each labelled and backed by evidence. The case saves itself as you go.

tryit.prompt: Is each one a note or a finding?
items: The parcel was collected at 09:30 true time (EV-005).

sandbox.task: Record one finding that cites at least one item.

steps.label: Add a finding with a citation

check.q: What makes a finding different from a note?
options: Findings are labelled and cite evidence
Notes are shown to the case lead
check.hint: Think about what you would stand behind in a report.

check.q: Can a finding be marked as fact with no evidence?
check.hint: The program will not let you.

check.q: What happens if the program closes unexpectedly?
options: Your work up to the last autosave is kept
check.hint: Saves are written as you work.
